title: A Partitioned Log and Consumer Lag

cells.source:
# A Partitioned Log and Consumer Lag

Market data, orders and trade events in a bank or exchange usually flow through a **partitioned log**: Kafka, or a cloud cousin such as Amazon Kinesis or Azure Event Hubs. Producers append messages to a **topic**; the topic is split into **partitions**; a **consumer group** shares the partitions out, one consumer per partition at most, and each consumer works through its partitions in order.

The number everyone watches is **consumer lag**: how many messages are waiting. Lag means stale prices and late risk numbers. The question: **what makes lag grow, and does adding consumers always fix it?**

How the cells run:

- **The simulation is an HTML cell** that runs live from the sliders: move one and it starts again. Nothing here talks to a real Kafka; it is a model with the same rules.
- **JavaScript** runs the same model for 1 to 12 consumers and measures the lag.

> ✨ The code cells were written by an AI model from prompts, and each prompt is saved in its cell: press **✨** in a cell's header to see it.

Press **Run all**, then play with the sliders.

## 1. The topic and the group

> Controls, 900 pixels wide, two rows of two sliders: "Partitions" bound to kf_partitions, 1 to 12, default 6; "Consumers in the group" bound to kf_consumers, 1 to 12, default 6; "Messages produced per second" bound to kf_rate, 100 to 2,000 in steps of 100, default 600; and "Messages one consumer handles per second" bound to kf_speed, 50 to 1,000 in steps of 50, default 300.

- **Partitions** are the unit of parallelism: two consumers in one group never read the same partition.
- **A key always goes to the same partition** (here `hash(key) % partitions`), so all the messages for one symbol stay in order. That's the guarantee; the price is that a busy key makes a busy partition.

## 2. Watch the lag

> Simulate a Kafka-style topic second by second for 180 seconds, live from the sliders in nb: 12 keys with skewed traffic (30%, 18%, 12% … 2%), each key's messages going to partition hash(key) mod the partition count, a 3x burst from 40 to 60 seconds, consumers sharing the partitions round-robin with each handling a fixed number of messages a second, and consumer 0 crashing at 90 seconds with its partitions left waiting until the group rebalances at 100 seconds. Draw each partition as a bar of the messages waiting in it (red when far behind), with its share of the keys and a dot coloured by the consumer that owns it, and below, the total lag over time with the burst and crash marked. Play, pause and restart, with a speed choice, and restart whenever a slider moves. Dark theme.

- **The burst (40 to 60 s)** triples the traffic. Lag builds, then drains at the rate the consumers have to spare.
- **The crash (90 s)**: consumer 0 stops, but the group doesn't notice for 10 seconds (the *session timeout*), so its partitions get no reading at all. Then they're handed to the others.
- **Try 12 consumers with 6 partitions**: six of them sit idle. **Try 3 consumers**: watch which partitions turn red and stay red.

## What the run shows

With the default sliders (6 partitions, 600 messages a second, 300 per consumer):

| consumers | peak lag | lag at 180 s | caught up after the burst |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 88,080 | 88,080 | never |
| 3 | 43,760 | 43,760 | never |
| 5 | 14,040 | 14,040 | never |
| 6 | 12,480 | 120 | at 173 s |
| 7 to 12 | 12,480 | 120 | at 173 s |

- **Past 6 consumers, nothing changes.** With 6 partitions the 7th to 12th consumers get no partitions at all: the line on the chart goes flat. Partitions set the ceiling on parallelism, so they're chosen up front for the biggest load you expect.
- **The keys aren't spread evenly, so neither are the partitions.** The 12 keys land 39%, 29%, 14%, 12% and 6% on five partitions and nothing on the sixth. The busiest partition gets 234 messages a second; a consumer handles 300.
- **One hot partition sets the recovery time.** After the burst, partition 1 can only drain at 300 − 234 = 66 messages a second, so even 6 consumers take until 173 s to catch up. Adding consumers can't help a single partition.
- **Too few consumers and lag never stops growing.** With 3 consumers, one of them owns partitions 1 and 4: 68% of the traffic, 408 messages a second against its 300. At 97 s it is 26,796 messages behind, and still falling further behind.
- **A crash costs a whole session timeout.** For 10 seconds after consumer 0 stops, the group doesn't know, and its partitions are read by nobody.


## Try this

Each of these is a prompt. Press **✨** in a cell's header to change its prompt and generate it again, or **⚡ AI Generate New Cell** at the bottom to add a new one.

- **Predict, then slide.** With 6 partitions, will 8 consumers clear the backlog faster than 6? Move the sliders and run the sweep.
- **Fix the hot key.** Press ✨ on the HTML cell and add: *"Split the busiest key into 4 sub-keys (ACME-0 to ACME-3), so its traffic spreads over several partitions."* What does that do to ordering for ACME?
- **A faster rebalance.** Press ✨ on the HTML cell and change the session timeout from 10 seconds to 3. How much lower is the lag after the crash?
- **Autoscale.** Press ✨ on the HTML cell and add: *"Add a consumer whenever total lag passes 5,000 messages, up to the number of partitions."*
- **Understand the code.** Press the speech bubble (**Explain this cell**) on the HTML cell and ask why a consumer group can't use more consumers than partitions.
